name: Account Erasure with Write Fencing
summary: Erase an authorised account's indexed service data while invalidating stale sessions and fencing already admitted work from restoring deleted state.
problem: Successful deletion or session rejection alone can leave older in-flight work able to recreate records or credentials after the account is erased.
coreOutcomes: Scoped deletion with separate registry and credential fences
Consequence-time rejection of stale admitted writes
Synthetic race acceptance distinct from real customer cleanup
requirements: Explicit account-deletion authority and identity confirmation
Canonical indexed inventory and active-work state
Generation or equivalent durable write guards
Safe fixture isolation and post-deletion read access
boundaries: Session invalidation alone does not prove stale-write rejection
Indexed service deletion is not external-account or key revocation
Unknown unindexed records retain their documented limitation
A service receipt is not an independent verifier verdict
